title.value: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies
title.justification: The title provides a clear and concise indication of the paper's focus on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence in Africa based on a meta-analysis.
title.quote: SARS-­CoV-­2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-­analysis of standardized seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021

extractions.description: This paper provides a systematic review and meta-analysis of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence studies conducted in Africa from January 2020 to December 2021. It aims to estimate seroprevalence to inform public health and vaccine strategies amid low vaccine coverage and challenges in routine surveillance. The study evaluates the extent of undetected infections by comparing seroprevalence with confirmed case data.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: Although the paper focuses on public health and the epidemiological study of SARS-CoV-2 in Africa, it does not directly address themes of climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Estimating COVID-­19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies.

primary_category.justification: The paper is primarily concerned with public health and epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in Africa. It does not focus on climate or ecologically-related sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: We undertook a meta-­analysis of population-­based seroprevalence studies to estimate SARS-­CoV-­2 seroprevalence in Africa to inform evidence-­based decision making on public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategy.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes in the paper that align with climate or ecologically-related sustainable development categories.
secondary_categories.quote: Estimating COVID-­19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category of climate or ecologically-related sustainable development is addressed, as the paper centers on viral epidemiology and seroprevalence study reviews.
primary_sub_category.quote: We estimated the extent of undetected infections by comparing seroprevalence and cumulative incidence of confirmed cases reported to WHO.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainability are addressed in the context of this paper.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We conducted descriptive analyses of seroprevalence and meta-­analysed seroprevalence differences by demographic groups, place and time.

applications.value: Informing public health and vaccination strategies
applications.justification: The paper's meta-analysis aims to provide insights for evidence-based decision making on public health and vaccine strategies in Africa.
applications.quote: Our results indicate a high seroprevalence in Africa (65.1%) in July–September 2021, which had increased from 3.0% in April–June 2020, and large, persistent under-­ascertainment of infection based on confirmed case-based data.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new category as the paper does not relate to climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: We report high seroprevalence in Africa suggesting greater population exposure to SARS-­CoV-­2 and potential protection against COVID-­19 severe disease than indicated by surveillance data.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not introduce new concepts relevant to sustainable development in relation to climate or ecology.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: To date, the pandemic has progressed in four major waves, with the most recent wave largely due to the Omicron variant circulating in a number of countries.
